items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: I met Lester Young, the great tenor saxophone player, and Joe Jones, in Omaha, Nebraska, while I was playing with Nat Towles.

ctx.x: Some of them who may not be as well equipped to play solo, they like to back up the good players, you see. So part of the inspiration and fun had sort of diminished in Nat Towles' band, and at that time then I was trying always to move on to better things, and I met Lester Young, the great tenor saxophone player, and Joe Jones, in Omaha, Nebraska, while I was playing with Nat Towles. Because Count Basie at this time now had became famous, and his music was becoming famous, and the players in his band became…

musicians at any chance that they got. And so by meeting Lester Young and Joe Jones, I was inspired, and as I was inspired naturally you wanted to go onto better things. And none of these orchestras that I played with had a full amount of men who were qualified to be good players.
